Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Hospitals Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Hospitals Inc.'s financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Medical Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Strategy Officer; and James Patel, Chief Information Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter of 2024. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on seven key aspects: same-facility admissions and patient day growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter; strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year; capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion; impact of seasonality or external factors such as flu season; initiatives to improve operating margin; percentage of revenue from Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and self-pay; and labor costs as a percentage of revenue.

These metrics highlight our organic momentum and disciplined approach in a challenging environment. For instance, we saw solid volume growth in same-facility admissions, and our payer mix remains balanced to support reimbursement stability. I'll touch on these briefly before handing over to David for a deeper financial review.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to David Thompson to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

David Thompson:
Thank you, Dr. Reynolds. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Net revenue for the second quarter of 2024 was $2.8 billion, an increase of 7.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Let me start by diving deeper into our same-facility admissions and patient days growth, which really underscores the strength of our core inpatient operations amid a shifting healthcare environment. As a quick reminder, these same-facility metrics strip out the effects of our recent small acquisitions, such as the joint venture with three community hospitals in the Midwest, and zero in on our 45 owned and operated facilities across the country. They're pure measures of our organic volume progress.

On a year-over-year basis, same-facility admissions rose 3.2% in the quarter, picking up speed from the 2.8% in the first quarter. Quarter-over-quarter, there was a 1.5% sequential increase, improving on the 1.1% from last year's first to second quarter transition. This flowed through to same-facility patient days growing 4.1% year-over-year—our best quarterly result since the fourth quarter of 2022—and 2.0% quarter-over-quarter. For perspective, our average length of stay remained stable at 4.7 days, and our case mix index climbed 1.8% year-over-year to 1.92, showing a positive move toward more complex cases. Our average daily census network-wide increased to 18,400 from 17,700 a year earlier.

Breaking down the drivers, admissions growth was widespread but strongest in cardiology and orthopedics, which drove 45% of the year-over-year gain. Elective procedures, still recovering from the 2022 Omicron impacts, jumped 6.5% year-over-year, powered by backlog demand for hip and knee replacements—now 15% above pre-pandemic baselines. Medical admissions increased 4.2%, with sepsis and pneumonia cases up 12%, matching CDC patterns for seasonal respiratory issues. Patient days outpaced admissions growth thanks to that CMI lift; we're securing higher MS-DRG weights in advanced cardiac work like TAVR and MitraClip, where volumes rose 22% year-over-year, in line with what HCA Healthcare has reported.

By region, our Sunbelt markets led the way. Facilities in Texas and Florida posted 5.8% year-over-year admissions growth, aided by population influx and strong payer mixes heavy in commercial and Medicare Advantage, bolstered by expanded Optum partnerships for bundled payments. Our Northeast urban sites encountered some resistance, with flat quarter-over-quarter growth from post-pandemic Medicaid redeterminations; New York and Massachusetts locations dipped 2% in patient days due to softer commercial acuity. California held firm with value-based care pilots stabilizing volumes at 1.2% year-over-year via shared savings with Blue Shield, despite Medi-Cal payment delays.

To keep this going, we've rolled out Epic's AI-driven patient flow tools enterprise-wide, reaching 85% of facilities by quarter-end, cutting discharge delays 18% and improving bed turnover by 1.2 turns daily—adding 0.8 points to quarter-over-quarter patient days. Cerner integrations have sharpened OR scheduling for high-CMI cases, lifting ortho case mix by 0.15 points. Our site-neutral care push hasn't hurt inpatient yet; outpatient grew 12% year-over-year, while complex cases like neuro-oncology in our Varian proton therapy joint venture added 7% to patient days.

Moving ahead, we anticipate third-quarter same-facility admissions at 2.5-3.0% year-over-year, patient days at 3.5-4.0%, accounting for flu pressures and election-related Medicare rate uncertainty. Our $250 million capital plan for 20 new hybrid ORs and tele-ICU builds sets us up to beat industry norms, similar to Tenet's path.

Our operating expenses were $2.45 billion, representing 87.5% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in labor optimization and supply chain efficiencies.

Net income for the quarter was $210 million, or $1.62 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Now, let's turn to our payer revenue mix, which provides insight into our reimbursement resilience. Across our 45 acute care hospitals and freestanding ERs, mainly in the Southeast and Midwest, the mix for the quarter was Medicare at 48.2% of net revenue, up 210 basis points from 46.1% in the prior year; Medicaid at 21.7%, down slightly 50 basis points; commercial insurance at 24.1%, off 110 basis points; and self-pay/other at 6.0%, up from 5.5% due to higher-acuity uninsured in Texas and Florida.

These net figures follow contractual adjustments, verified through our HIMSS Stage 7 EMR and Epic revenue cycle systems. The Medicare increase tracks national trends with a 4.1% rise in FFS admissions per CMS, amplified by 6.3% growth in observation and outpatient under OPPS, like IR and cath lab. Medicare Advantage hit 42% penetration in our markets, contributing 22% of Medicare revenue, with rates at 98% of FFS though delegated risk deals in three areas add upside.

Medicaid stability came from expansion states like Kentucky and Louisiana, offset by softer managed care in Indiana. Commercial faced unit cost pushback from Blues and Cigna, with ASP per discharge down 1.8% to $14,200, but renewals captured 3-4% lifts in most contracts. Self-pay rose with electives, improved by AI eligibility checks boosting cash to 92%.

Regionally, Southeast has Medicare at 52%, Medicaid 25%; Midwest commercial 32%, Medicaid 18%; Texas self-pay 9%. Our RCM investments cut denials 28%, especially MA auths, and value-based pilots with Humana target capitation.

Labor costs warrant specific attention as our biggest expense line. For the quarter, they stood at 55.8% of revenue, up 210 basis points year-over-year from 53.7% but steady sequentially. Absolute spend rose 8.2% to $1.42 billion, from 6.5% wage hikes—RNs at $48.20/hour—and premium pay at 12% of total, improved from 14%.

Vacancies at 11-13% mirror AHA data, worsened by burnout and competitors like Optum. Admissions up 4.1%, CMI 1.85 added HPPD to 10.8. Sunbelt at 54.2%, West Coast 59.4% from wage laws, rural Midwest 53.1%.

Mitigations include Oracle Health scheduling for 18% better fills, 22% less overtime; ApexCare AI forecasting census, cutting agency 25%; $150 million retention with bonuses, tuition, lifting retention to 87%. We're upper quartile vs. Tenet, CHS. Expect moderation to 55.0-55.5% Q3, 54.5% full year.

On initiatives boosting operating margin, we hit 7.2% this quarter, up 140 basis points to best since pre-pandemic, adding $285 million operating income on $4.2 billion revenue—wait, quarterly context $2.8B. On pace for 7.5-8.0% full year, eyeing 9% by 2026 like HCA.

Via MarginMax yielding $450M run-rate savings: labor 42% impact—admissions per bed 1.18, Cerner AI cut agency to 6.5%, HPPD 8.2; retention programs dropped turnover 22%; labor % to 50.8%. Supply 28%—Premier GPO 12-15% off, zero-based implants knee to $5,600, hubs cut logistics 11%; supply to 14.2%. RCM 20%—denials to 4.8%, Epic capture $2.50/day, payer uplifts commercial to 58%; rev/adm $14,200. Capacity 10%—utilization 68%, 15 ASCs.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Chen for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Lisa Chen:
Thank you, David. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our value-based care programs have delivered promising results, including a 15% reduction in readmissions in pilot sites. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, now at 35% of outpatient visits, and remote patient monitoring programs that integrate AI predictive analytics from Nuance to support higher acuity management.

Following that, Robert will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including Epic's AI patient flow modules reducing delays and Cerner's predictive OR scheduling, alongside regional supply hubs with Vizient GPO yielding $22 million savings year-to-date. These have resulted in significant cost savings, better patient flow, and resilience against external factors.

Speaking of which, seasonality and outside influences like the flu season impacted dynamics positively this quarter, though Q2 is milder. Historically, winter quarters see surges—in Q4 last year, admissions rose 14% from high-severity flu in 17 states per CDC, ED volumes 18% to 2.1M with 32% respiratory, patient days 12% to 1.85M, CMI 1.85. Acute revenue $2.4B up 9.2%. Northeast/Midwest up 21%, Sunbelt softer. El Niño added trauma, RSV peds 28%. AI forecasting enabled bed surges, telehealth diverted 18% low-acuity, premium labor down 12%. Prepped for Q1 2025 with ICU expansions, vaccine pacts.

Next, Emily will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Emily Vargas:
Thank you, Robert. Our strategic priorities center on operational excellence and margin expansion, clinical and digital transformation, inorganic growth through M&A, and geographic expansion into high-growth markets—positioning us to lead.

On excellence, RN turnover to 14.2% via $15M incentives, labor % to 48.1%, Vizient savings $22M. Q3 admissions 3.5-4.5%, revenue $2.15-2.20B. Electives near pre-pandemic.

Digital: 28% risk-bearing revenue, Optum ACO 150K lives $18M savings, Epic MyChart 85%, robotics 65% util CMI 1.92. 2025 $250M capex for R1 RCM, AR to 45 days, telehealth 35%.

M&A: $1.2B powder, closed $450M three-hospital DFW deal accretive 15¢ EPS, now 12 Texas sites. Pipeline 15-20 Midwest tuck-ins for aging demo.

Expansion: Southeast 55% EBITDA 5.2% growth, MA 42%; Phoenix 200-bed $180M Q4 groundbreak. Full year revenue $8.6-8.8B, EBITDA $1.15-1.20B 13.0-13.5%, EPS $4.80-5.00. 2025 6-8% growth.

On capex for modernization/expansion, Q2 $285M up 18%, YTD $780M toward $1.05-1.15B full year, 5.2% revenue. 65% modernization $185M: 12 Siemens 3T MRIs, 8 GE CTs throughput +20%, Epic AI $45M doc time -12%, Trane HVAC $37M energy -18%.

Expansion 35% $100M: San Antonio 120-bed +24 ICU/4 hybrid ORs CMI to 2.05; Boston ASC $25M USPI JV; Midwest tele-ICU $15M. IRR 15-20%, funded 70% FCF $420M Q2. Q4 $260-280M.

After that, James will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

James Patel:
Thank you, Emily. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures, including advanced AI-driven threat detection from Oracle Health and Nuance integrations, multi-factor authentication across Epic systems, and regular penetration testing. Our cybersecurity posture has strengthened with zero major incidents this year, ensuring HIPAA compliance and resilience against rising threats.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of the recent cybersecurity threats on your operations and patient data?

James Patel:
Good morning, John. Recent threats haven't disrupted our operations, thanks to proactive measures. We've enhanced our defenses with Epic-integrated AI analytics that detect anomalies 88% faster, regular third-party audits, and employee training reaching 95% completion. Patient data remains secure, with encryption standards exceeding HIPAA and no breaches reported. This aligns with our $50 million annual IT security budget, positioning us ahead of industry averages.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mary Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mary Johnson:
What are your plans for expanding your telehealth capabilities and remote patient monitoring programs?

Dr. Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Mary. We're aggressively scaling telehealth to 35% of outpatients by year-end, building on 45% growth in virtual urgent care that diverted low-acuity cases last flu season. RPM integrates Philips eICU and Nuance AI for real-time monitoring, reducing readmissions 15% in pilots. Partnerships like Optum expand to ACO REACH, targeting 200,000 lives. Capex supports hybrid ORs and MyChart enhancements for seamless care.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Lee:
Can you provide more details on your strategic partnerships and their potential impact on your business?

Emily Vargas:
Hi Alex. Partnerships drive our pillars. Optum and Humana for ACO/value-based, yielding $18M savings; Vizient GPO $22M supply savings; USPI ASC JV tapping 15% CAGR; Varian proton, GSK vaccines. Recent Tenet DFW acquisition accretive immediately. These boost margins 100-300 bps, revenue 5-7%, de-risk payer shifts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel:
David, can you elaborate on labor cost trends and margin outlook given ongoing shortages?

David Thompson:
Sure, Chris. Labor at 55.8% reflects inflation but stabilizing via AI scheduling and retention—turnover 14%, agency down to 6.5%. Margin initiatives like MarginMax target 7.5-8% full year, with productivity KPIs like $142 revenue per hour. Q3 moderation expected, supporting EBITDA expansion.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Hospitals Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
